subject: physics
title: Photon Cannon
summary: Fire photons at a metal: find the faintest light that frees an electron, the voltage that stops it, and h from a line.

chapter.name: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

ncertRef: Section 11.6, Einstein’s photoelectric equation: energy quantum of radiation
concepts: The V₀–f line and Planck’s constant
learningOutcome: The student can find the threshold wavelength hc/φ, the maximum kinetic energy hf − φ and the stopping potential, and read h and φ from a straight V₀–f line.

levels.title: Zap’s threshold
levels.adds: Baseline: one photon frees one electron only if hf is at least the work function, so the threshold wavelength is hc/φ (Ex 11.6 to 11.8).
hints: An electron escapes only if one photon carries at least φ: hc/λ ≥ φ.
The faintest light that works has hc/λ = φ, so λ = 1240 eV nm / φ.
Brighter light of a longer wavelength still frees nothing.

levels.title: Volt’s stopping potential
levels.adds: New idea: the fastest electron has K_max = hf − φ and is just stopped by eV₀ = K_max (Ex 11.2, 11.3, 11.9; Example 11.2).
hints: Photon energy is 1240 eV nm divided by the wavelength in nm.
K_max = photon energy − work function, in eV.
The stopping potential in volts is the same number as K_max in eV.

levels.title: Ruler’s line
levels.adds: Apply it: V₀ = (h/e) f − φ/e is a straight line, so two points give both h (the slope) and φ (the intercept) (Ex 11.5).
hints: The slope between the points is ΔV₀/Δf = h/e, so h = e × slope.
Convert the units: Δf is in 10¹⁴ Hz, so h comes out in units of 10⁻³⁴ J s once you use e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.
Then φ = hf₁ − eV₁ for either point.

misconceptions: Brighter light of any colour can free electrons from a metal
The stopping potential grows with the intensity of the light
The kinetic energy of the electrons is hf
